bodies.name: Chiron
bodies.identity: One physical body with two catalogue identities. JPL SBDB returns the same record for sstr=2060 and sstr=95P: des 2060, spkid 20002060, fullname '2060 Chiron (1977 UB)', kind 'an' (numbered asteroid), des_alt [{pri: 1977 UB}, {com: 95P}], orbit class CEN (Centaur). cssEarth registers one scene.
bodies.axisUncertaintyNote: Full-axis uncertainties are the published semiaxis uncertainties 22, 19 and 13 km doubled. They are not independent.
bodies.axesStatus: Three semiaxes from one published model fit, not three independently measured axes. The reference radius is the geometric mean of the model semiaxes; it is the rendering scale and it agrees with the paper's volume-equivalent radius 98 ± 17 km.

areaEquivalentRadiusKm.meaning: Apparent area-equivalent radius, held fixed in the occultation fit; taken from the radiometric diameter of Lellouch et al. 2017 (A&A 608, A45).

bodies.credit: Braga-Ribas et al. (2023), Astronomy & Astrophysics 676, A72; 2019 September 8 multi-chord stellar occultation
bodies.shapeMeaning: Published triaxial figure from the 2019 September 8 multi-chord stellar occultation: semiaxes 126 ± 22, 109 ± 19 and 68 ± 13 km, volume-equivalent radius 98 ± 17 km (Braga-Ribas et al. 2023, A&A 676, A72). Only the apparent limb ellipse is fitted from the chords. The third axis follows from three stated assumptions: a Jacobi fluid-equilibrium figure at the 5.917813 h rotation period, the true light-curve amplitude 0.16 ± 0.03 mag of Groussin et al. 2004, and a body pole assumed equal to the Ortiz et al. 2015 ring pole. The area-equivalent radius was held fixed at 105 (+6/-7) km, the radiometric value of Lellouch et al. 2017, so the scale is radiometric, not occultation-measured. This is a model figure, not resolved terrain.
bodies.orientationMeaning: Illustrative ICRF north pole (right ascension 0 degrees, declination +90 degrees), arbitrary prime meridian and phase. Chiron has no measured spin pole. The published ring or disk pole near ecliptic longitude 151 degrees, latitude +20 degrees is a pole of the surrounding material; the shape paper assumes the body shares it, and this display does not adopt that assumption as an orientation.
bodies.surfaceMeaning: Unmapped surface: the standard grid is a coordinate aid, not observed colour or terrain. Chiron is about 0.015 arcsec across at its current distance and has never been resolved.

colour.meaning: MBOSS-2 weighted means. The spectral gradient is measured against the solar spectrum, so 0.1 ± 1.0 percent per 100 nm means Chiron's reflectance is solar-coloured within its errors. The shared neutral material is used rather than a derived display colour, because a colour derived from these indices would be indistinguishable from neutral and the indices mix nucleus and coma across 34 epochs of varying activity.

bodies.introduction: Kowal found Chiron beyond Saturn in 1977, the first Centaur known. It later grew a coma, so one body carries both an asteroid number and a comet designation.
bodies.card: The first known Centaur, and a comet as well.
bodies.datasetSummary: A 252 × 218 × 136 km figure from one occultation outline and an assumed equilibrium shape.
